pages.layout: Two large top panels (captain thanking her crew vs. Poppy's shocked reaction) sit side by side with a small teal inset -- the dropped treasure chest, DROP/BLAG SFX -- wedged into the gutter between them, overlapping both frames' lower edges. Below that, the outer panel borders drop away entirely: the lower two-thirds of the page becomes one continuous blue lightning-cracked background occupied by Poppy's trembling clenched fists in extreme foreground. Two small bordered insets (the captain's mid-left 'discreet' panel, then a bottom-left captain-laughing panel) float on top of that borderless backdrop, stacked vertically, so the dialogue panels and the mood-backdrop panel are literally layered rather than placed side by side. No panel bleeds to the trimmed page edge; the two chest-drop and laugh insets are the only bordered shapes sitting directly against the unframed backdrop with no white gutter of their own.
pages.reading_flow: Reads left-to-right across the top row (captain speaks, then Poppy reacts), but the inset chest panel breaks strict L-to-R order by sitting in the gutter between the two top panels -- the eye detours into it (and its DROP/BLAG SFX) after Poppy's first 'I uh but but...' bubble and before her second 'HOW?!' bubble. From there the page steps down to the captain's explanation panel at mid-left, then across the gutter onto Poppy's trembling-fist backdrop (her defiant declaration bubble sits high in that field, roughly level with the captain panel beside it), and finally back down-left to the captain's mocking-laugh inset at the very bottom, stacked directly under the 'discreet' panel and floating on the same fist backdrop. The layered inset-on-backdrop device (panels 3 and 6 both sit inside/on top of a larger unframed field rather than beside it) is the convention break worth flagging.

signature_moves.move: Low-hero flex ladder: the same front double-biceps pose redrawn at escalating panel scale across a page
signature_moves.steal_for_cgi: Generate the identical camera height/crop/pose across 3 consecutive panels, only scaling the figure and adding incremental pose/expression variation panel to panel -- do not copy-paste the render.

signature_moves.move: Extreme close-up on a single growing body part, frame-cropped with zero or minimal background
signature_moves.steal_for_cgi: Push the lens tight enough that the muscle/mass fills the frame edge-to-edge with a plain or blurred field behind it; pair with a cut-in face reaction panel so the beat doesn't go faceless.

signature_moves.move: Near-universal diagonal panel energy -- even quiet dialogue beats are staged off a raked axis
signature_moves.steal_for_cgi: Default every panel's composition line (body axis, prop, horizon) to a diagonal rather than a level line, even for non-growth panels.

signature_moves.move: Cloth-strain and tear sfx-paired growth (STRETCHHHH / RIIIP / SNAP) escalating panel to panel
signature_moves.steal_for_cgi: Stage visible fabric tension lines / a torn seam at the exact point the muscle is meant to be selling growth, escalating garment damage across consecutive panels.

signature_moves.steal_for_cgi: Compose one normal-scale figure and one grown figure in the same shot at different camera depths to sell size without needing a measured prop.

avoid: Stacked repeated onomatopoeia (BULGE BULGE BULGE, SWELL SWELL SWELL) doing the primary work of selling an off-panel or faceless growth beat (p13 panels 3-4, p16 panels 1-2) -- a photoreal panel has no text layer to lean on; the pose, tension, and lighting have to carry what the sfx repetition carries here.

Muscle mass literally breaking the panel's own border (p8 panel 4, p14 panel 4: 'muscles now crowd past the panel's own borders') -- a 2D page-layout trick with no single-camera equivalent; substitute an extreme frame-crop where the mass fills the lens instead.

Verbatim panel-to-panel pose repeats used as the entire escalation mechanism (p8 panels 2-4, p14 panels 2-4 redraw the identical double-bicep pose bigger each time) -- cheap in ink where the linework alone reads as 'bigger'; a CGI render needs genuine incremental pose/expression/tension change or the sequence reads as a lazy re-render, not escalation.

Grayscale/desaturation used as a reveal device (p2 panel 4, the silhouette-captain cliffhanger) -- a stylistic ink trick for mood; in a photoreal pipeline a sudden desaturated panel would read as a color-grade bug, not a deliberate reveal.

Nested, non-standard panel borders bleeding into an unbordered energy backdrop (p3's layered insets floating on a borderless lightning-cracked background) -- a page-layout composition device with no single-panel photoreal equivalent; skip for per-panel generation.
